data.content_ref: inline:The transfer's core mechanism is inadmissible for sorting networks. The analogy borrows an inversion-count lower bound from adjacent-transposition permutation sorting, but the target itself flags (in disanalogies) that sorting-network comparators can act on non-adjacent channels. Because a single comparator between channels i,j (|i-j|>1) can resolve multiple inversions at once, the adjacent-transposition inversion count is NOT a valid lower bound on the number of remaining comparators. Using it as a branch-and-bound pruning rule would overestimate remaining work and could prune branches that actually contain optimal S(n) networks — directly violating the requirement that a pruning rule preserve optimality at small n. The target acknowledges this disanalogy but never resolves whether the bound remains admissible; the simulation overturn conditions test empirical utility but not admissibility, so the rule may be unsound even if it appears to prune well in tested cases.
